ཤེས་པ་སྐྱེ་བར་འགྱུར། །མིག་#དང་གཟུགས་དང་རྣམ་པར་ཤེས། །གསུམ་པོ་འདུས་པ་གང་ཡིན་པ། །དེ་ནི་རེག་པའོ་རེག་དེ་ལས། །ཚོར་བ་ཀུན་ཏུ་འབྱུང་བར་འགྱུར། །ཚོར་བའི་རྐྱེན་གྱིས་སྲེད་པ་སྟེ། །ཚོར་བའི་དོན་དུ་སྲེད་པར་འགྱུར། །སྲེད་
པར་གྱུར་ན་ཉེ་བར་ལེན། །རྣམ་པ་བཞི་པོ་ཉེར་ལེན་འགྱུར། །ཉེར་ལེན་ཡོད་ན་ལེན་པ་པོའི། །སྲིད་པ་རབ་ཏུ་འབྱུང་བར་འགྱུར། །གལ་ཏེ་ཉེ་བར་ལེན་མེད་ན། །གྲོལ་བར་འགྱུར་ཏེ་སྲིད་མི་འགྱུར། །སྲིད་པ་དེ་ཡང་ཕུང་པོ་ལྔ། །སྲིད་པ་ལས་ནི་སྐྱེ་
བར་འགྱུར#། །རྒ་ཤི་དང་ནི་མྱ་ངན་དང་། །སྨྲེ་སྔགས་འདོན་བཅས་སྡུག་བསྔལ་དང་། །ཡིད་མི་བདེ་དང་འཁྲུག་པ་རྣམས། །དེ་དག་སྐྱེ་ལས་རབ་ཏུ་འབྱུང་། །དེ་ལྟར་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ཕུང་པོ་ནི། །འབའ་ཞིག་པ་#འདི་འབྱུང་བར་འགྱུར། །འཁོར་བའི་
རྩ་བ་འདུ་བྱེད་དེ། །དེ་ཕྱིར་མཁས་རྣམས་འདུ་མི་བྱེད། །དེ་ཕྱིར་མི་མཁས་བྱེད་པོ་ཡིན། །མཁས་མིན་#དེ་ཉིད་མཐོང་ཕྱིར་རོ། །མ་རིག་འགགས་པར་གྱུར་ན་ནི། །འདུ་བྱེད་རྣམས་ཀྱང་འབྱུང་མི་འགྱུར། །མ་རིག་འགག་པར་འགྱུར་བ་ནི། །ཤེས་
པས་དེ་ཉིད་བསྒོམས་པས་སོ། །དེ་དང་དེ་ནི་འགགས་གྱུར་པས། །དེ་དང་དེ་ནི་མངོན་#མི་འབྱུང་། །སྡུག་བསྔལ་ཕུང་པོ་འབའ་ཞིག་པ#། །དེ་ནི་དེ་ལྟར་ཡང་དག་འགག །སྲིད་པའི་ཡན་ལག་བཅུ་གཉིས་བརྟག་པ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་སྟེ་རབ་ཏུ་བྱེད་པ་ཉི་ཤུ་དྲུག་
པའོ།། །།འདས་དུས་བྱུང་མ་བྱུང་ཞེས་དང་། །འཇིག་རྟེན་རྟག་པ་ལ་སོགས་པར། །ལྟ་བ་གང་ཡིན་དེ་དག་ནི། །མངོན་#གྱི་མཐའ་ལ་བརྟེན་པ་ཡིན། །མ་འོངས་དུས་གཞན་འབྱུང་འགྱུར་#དང་། །མི་འབྱུང་འཇིག་རྟེན་མཐའ་སོགས་པར། །ལྟ་
བ་གང་ཡིན་དེ་དག་ནི། །ཕྱི་མའི་མཐའ་ལ་བརྟེན་པ་ཡིན། །འདས་པའི་དུས་ན་བྱུང་གྱུར་ཞེས། །བྱ་བ་དེ་ནི་མི་འཐད་དོ། །སྔོན་ཚེ་རྣམས་སུ་གང་བྱུང་བ། །དེ་ཉིད་འདི་ནི་མ་ཡིན་ནོ། །དེ་ཉིད་བདག་ཏུ་འགྱུར་སྙམ་ན། །ཉེ་བར་ལེན་

consciousness arises. The meeting of the three—eye, form, and consciousness—is contact. From that contact, feeling arises. Craving is conditioned by feeling; one craves for the sake of feeling. When there is craving, grasping occurs; the four types of grasping occur. When there is grasping, the existence of the grasper comes to be. If there is no grasping, one is liberated and existence does not occur. That existence is the five aggregates; from existence, birth arises. Aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, mental unease, and agitation all arise from birth. Thus, this whole mass of suffering arises. Karmic formations are the root of cyclic existence; therefore, the wise do not perform them. The unwise are the performers, because the wise see reality. When ignorance has ceased, karmic formations will not arise. The cessation of ignorance comes from meditating on reality with knowledge. Through the ceasing of this and that, this and that do not manifest. The whole mass of suffering thus completely ceases. This was the twenty-sixth chapter, titled "The Investigation of the Twelve Links of Existence."

Views such as whether one existed or did not exist in the past, or whether the world is permanent and so on, depend on the prior limit. Views such as whether one will exist or not exist in the future, or whether the world is finite and so on, depend on the future limit. The claim that one existed in the past is not tenable. <meta>continues from previous page</meta>
...consciousness will arise. Eye, form, and consciousness—the meeting of these three is contact. From that contact, feeling arises in every way. Conditioned by feeling is craving; for the sake of feeling, one craves. When craving occurs, grasping follows; the four types of grasping arise. When grasping exists, the becoming <note>existence</note> of the grasper comes into being. If there is no grasping, one is liberated and becoming does not occur. That becoming is the five aggregates; from becoming, birth arises. Aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, mental unhappiness, and disturbances—all these arise from birth. Thus, this entire mass of suffering comes into being. 

Formations are the root of <term>samsara</term> <gloss>cyclic existence</gloss>; therefore, the wise do not form them. Because they are not wise, the ignorant are the performers of actions; for they do not see reality. If ignorance is ceased, formations will not arise either. The cessation of ignorance occurs through the cultivation of knowledge of reality. Through the cessation of this and that, this and that will not manifest. The entire mass of suffering is thus completely ceased.

This was the twenty-sixth chapter, titled "Examination of the Twelve Links of Existence."

### Chapter 27: Examination of Views

Views such as "I existed in the past" or "I did not exist," or whether the world is "permanent" and so on, depend on the former limit <note>past existence</note>. Views such as "I will exist in a different future time" or "I will not exist," or whether the world has an "end" and so on, depend on the later limit <note>future existence</note>.

To say "I existed in a past time" is not tenable. That which existed in former times is not this very same one <note>the person now</note>. If you think "That itself has become the self," then apart from grasping <note>the five aggregates</note>, what is your self? If it is established that there is no self apart from grasping, then if grasping itself were the self, your self would be non-existent <note>because grasping is transient</note>. 

Grasping itself is not the self; it is characterized by arising and perishing. How could that which is grasped be the grasper? The self is not tenable as being other than the grasping. If it were other, it should be perceivable without grasping, yet it is not perceivable. Thus, it is neither other than grasping, nor is it the grasping itself. The self is not without grasping, but it is also not certain that it exists as a non-entity.

To say "I did not exist in a past time" is also not tenable. This one <note>the current person</note> is not different from that which existed in former times. If this were different, it would have arisen even without that one. Likewise, it would be permanent, and birth would occur without death there. Annihilation, the loss of actions <note>karma</note>, the experience by one of the actions performed by another, and such consequences would follow. It does not arise from what did not previously exist; this would lead to errors here. The self would be something created, or it would be something without a cause. 

Thus, views concerning the past—that the self arose, did not arise, both, or neither—are not tenable. 

Views regarding whether one will arise in a different future time or will not arise are identical to those regarding the past.
